title: Codex Linux seccomp checks did not cover x32 syscall numbers
summary: The x32 ABI shares the x86-64 audit architecture, so an architecture check alone did not apply Codex syscall restrictions to x32 callers. A fix applies the existing syscall denials and socket-family conditions to x32 syscall numbers and legacy aliases.

severity.rationale: The flaw weakens a coding assistant sandbox boundary for an alternate Linux ABI. It requires an environment capable of executing x32 calls; the inspected sources do not establish a complete sandbox escape.

affected.note: The 0.171.0 release includes the fix. The inspected sources do not establish the introduced version or a complete affected range.

exposure: Linux x86-64 sandbox execution using x32 syscall numbers can evade checks that only consider native syscall numbers. The fix covers seccomp syscall and socket-family rules, not a demonstrated bypass of every sandbox layer.

params.instructions: Check the Codex release and whether its Linux sandbox includes the x32 seccomp fix from the 0.171.0 release. Determine whether the kernel supports x32 execution; do not infer a full affected range from an older version alone.

remediation.details: Use release 0.171.0 or later containing the x32 seccomp fix.
remediation.risk: Low. Check existing sandboxed workflows after upgrading.

verification: Confirm the installed release includes the fix and run the vendor seccomp regression probes in an isolated development environment.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record of the vendor-documented x32 seccomp fix; affected-range and full-escape claims deliberately omitted.
